dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim with two views of the orthonormal DCT-II. The 1-D view shows the eight N = 8 basis functions, the coefficients of a preset or hand-drawn 8-sample signal, the reconstruction from the first K coefficients with its error, and the fraction of the energy captured by the first K DCT and DFT coefficients. The 2-D view shows the 64 basis images of the separable 8x8 DCT (C = D X D^T), a synthetic image block, uniform quantization with step Q that zeroes small coefficients, the reconstructed block, the pixel error and the PSNR.

learningObjectives: Describe the N = 8 DCT-II basis functions and relate the index k to the number of half-cycles of the cosine across the block
Calculate the fraction of the energy held by the first K DCT coefficients and use Parseval's relation to predict the energy of the reconstruction error
Compare the energy compaction of the DCT and the DFT for the same signal, and explain the difference with the mirror (even) extension versus the periodic extension
Apply uniform quantization with step Q to the 2-D DCT of an 8x8 block and relate the number of nonzero coefficients to the PSNR
Explain why JPEG transforms 8x8 blocks with the DCT before quantizing them
prerequisites: Definition of the DFT and Parseval's theorem

misconceptions.misconception: The DCT always compacts energy better than the DFT
misconceptions.correction: The DCT's advantage holds for smooth, correlated signals; a signal that is exactly periodic in the block, or an edge at some K, can favour the DFT
misconceptions.evidence: Cosine, one period with K = 3: DFT 100.00% vs DCT 96.33%; step edge with K = 3: DFT 85.36% vs DCT 82.11%

misconceptions.misconception: The highest-frequency DCT basis function is the alternating sequence (-1)^n
misconceptions.correction: phi_7 alternates in sign under a slow cosine envelope, so an alternating sequence spreads over the odd DCT coefficients
misconceptions.evidence: Alternating +-2: X[7] = 5.13 holds only 82.11% of the energy, with X[5] = 1.80, X[3] = 1.20 and X[1] = 1.02; the DFT puts all of it in bin 4

accessibility.screenReaderScript: DCT basis explorer with two views. 1-D view: eight small plots of the DCT-II basis functions for k = 0 to 7, a bar chart of the DCT coefficients of an 8-sample signal, the signal with its reconstruction from the first K coefficients, the reconstruction error, the DFT magnitudes of the same signal, and the fraction of the energy captured by the first K DCT and DFT coefficients. 2-D view: the 64 basis images of the 8 by 8 DCT, an 8 by 8 test block, its quantized coefficients, the reconstructed block, the error and the PSNR. Drop-down lists choose the view and the signal or block; sliders set K or the quantization step Q; click a basis function to highlight it and drag a sample to edit the 1-D signal.

controls.label: View
controls.description: Switches between the 1-D signal view (N = 8) and the 2-D 8x8 block view

controls.label: Signal
controls.description: Chooses the 8-sample signal x[n] in the 1-D view; dragging a sample switches it to custom

controls.label: Coefficients kept K
controls.description: Keeps the first K DCT coefficients (and the first K DFT bins in frequency order) in the 1-D view

controls.label: Block
controls.description: Chooses the synthetic 8x8 image block in the 2-D view

controls.label: Quantization step Q
controls.description: Uniform quantization step for the 2-D DCT coefficients: C becomes Q round(C/Q), so |C| < Q/2 becomes 0

visualElements.description: Eight small plots of the DCT-II basis functions phi_k[n] for k = 0..7 with their underlying cosines; kept ones maroon, dropped ones gray; click to highlight
Bar chart of the DCT coefficients X[k] with value labels; the first K are maroon, the rest gray, and the highlighted k has a gold outline
Signal x[n] (blue stems, draggable), reconstruction x_K[n] from the first K coefficients (purple curve and rings) and the contribution X[k] phi_k[n] of the highlighted basis function (gold dashed)
Error e[n] = x[n] - x_K[n] (red) with its energy, equal to the energy of the dropped coefficients
DFT magnitudes |X_DFT[k]|/sqrt(8) in frequency order 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, -3, 4, with the first K in green
Fraction of the energy in the first K coefficients versus K for the DCT (maroon) and the DFT (green), with the current K marked in gold (wide screens)
Grid of the 64 basis images of the 8x8 DCT; images whose quantized coefficient is 0 are faded; click to highlight one and read its coefficient
Original 8x8 block, quantized coefficient map (maroon, log scale), reconstructed block and |error| map (red), with hover read-outs of pixel and coefficient values
Energy fractions of the first K DCT and DFT coefficients; number of nonzero quantized coefficients, PSNR, MSE, maximum error and the energy share of the nonzero coefficients

model.description: Orthonormal DCT-II of an 8-sample signal and of an 8x8 block (level-shifted by 128). The 1-D view keeps the first K coefficients and compares the captured energy with the first K DFT bins in frequency order; the 2-D view quantizes every coefficient with a uniform step Q, inverts the transform, rounds and clips the pixels to 0..255 and reports the PSNR.
equations: X[k] = c_k sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] cos(pi k (2n + 1) / 2N), c_0 = sqrt(1/N), c_k = sqrt(2/N)
C = D X D^T, X = block - 128

instructionalStrategies: Predict which coefficients are zero from the symmetry of the signal
Increase K one step at a time and compare the DCT and DFT energy read-outs
Raise Q and watch the nonzero count and the PSNR fall for different blocks
extensions: Replace the uniform step with the JPEG luminance quantization table
Add zig-zag ordering and run-length coding of the quantized coefficients
